item.content:encoded:
Seconded on sword football being a legitimate variation that can be excused from containment, and that it needs to get more TV coverage.

So does ice rock football:

Quarterbacks slide a football made of granite down a narrow sheet of ice at a round endzone. Each possession lasts a single down, and balls from previous plays are only removed between the ten quarters of play. Only balls remaining in the endzone at the end of a quarter are scored. Receivers are not permitted to catch or contact the stone football, presumably due to risk of injury. Instead, they appear to remotely guide the stone football by using brooms to generate some form of inertial manipulation field.1 Balls left on the field fill the role of traditional defensive positions, and tackling of other balls with the ball in play is freely encouraged. Replacement of the ball, defensive positions, and offensive tackles with rocks has been deemed a novel addition to the standard ruleset; tests using D-class and stones of various sizes have been enthusiastically endorsed.

Footnotes
1. Possibly anomalous, research ongoing
